$comment: Content metadata owned by the content steward, not by developers.
Each entry becomes Azure Blob metadata at upload time, and the blob indexer
maps blob metadata into index fields of the same name automatically.
The 'status' value is what knowledge:filter selects on, so moving a document
from draft to approved is a metadata change rather than a code change.
IsDeleted is the soft-delete marker. The indexer's deletion detection policy
watches it, and it must exist from the very first indexer run.
Note on contoso-returns-policy-2027-draft.md: it is unapproved content, but
its body deliberately reads like a finished policy. The governance signal
lives in the status metadata here, not in the prose. An earlier version said
'must NOT be quoted to customers' inside the document, which the model read
as an instruction and refused to answer, hiding the very failure the scope
comparison exists to show: unapproved content produces a confident wrong
answer that looks exactly like a right one.
